answer: Each identity locks an 80-credit stake in the cedar ledger and owes three reviews per epoch, on an overlapping lattice: six reviewers per submission, three per reviewer, so clones share nothing. Within one point of crystal consensus is honest; a deviant review burns 20 credits. The kth fake needs a fresh 80-credit lock and three reviews; 1,000 fakes lock 80,000 credits and owe 3,000 reviews. A mill copying grades across clones or rating its own clones highly deviates and burns 20 credits per grade. Burned credits sink in the basalt pool. Honest agents lock once, lose nothing.
